 Plano ISD to use decommissioned city ambulance for EMT program at new center 
 Education Plano Plano ISD to use decommissioned city ambulance for EMT program at new center
 Explore Plano on the Impact Map stories, offers and more Patricia Ortiz 1 min read Published November 19, 2026 at 7:00 a.m. CT PISD's Career and Technical Education center will use decommissioned ambulances from the City of Plano for its Emergency Medical Technician program. (Patricia Ortiz/Community Impact) The city of Plano approved an agreement with Plano ISD to use a decommissioned ambulance for the district's Emergency Medical Technician, or EMT, program at a meeting Nov. 9.
 The details
 The decommissioned ambulance will be used to provide students with a hands-on training experience for emergency service and other healthcare fields, per city documents . 
 The district has already received the ambulance and is finalizing setup and safety preparations for the classroom, Plano ISD Communications Director Zoheb Hassanali said, with plans for students to start using the ambulance in the spring semester.
 The classes will be held at the new Career and Technical Education center the district opened Nov. 4 . Center classes were temporarily held at Academy High School while construction finished for the new facility located at the corner of Alma Drive and Park Boulevard, per previous reporting.
 “This opportunity provides our aspiring EMTs with invaluable, hands-on training that cannot be replicated in a traditional classroom," PISD Superintendent Theresa Williams said in an email. "By practicing real-life scenarios in an authentic setting, students develop the muscle memory, critical thinking and confidence required in the field. It is a prime example of work-based learning in action that prepares our students for immediate success in emergency medical careers.”
 The background
 The CTE center provides 19 career pathways for students in industries like health science, construction, manufacturing and more, per previous reporting. The new center was approved by voters as part of the district's $1.34 billion bond package in 2022.
 Construction for the $76 million CTE center started in 2023, according to the district, with unique teaching spaces like a hair salon, kitchen and shop area for welding.
